preamble.summary: Isaiah 38 records HEZEKIAH'S ILLNESS, divine-15-year-life-extension, and the SUNDIAL-SIGN (the shadow-going-back-ten-degrees on Ahaz's-sundial). The chapter contains a unique-poetic Hezekiah's-prayer (vv. 9–20) absent-from-2-Kings 20.
preamble.notable_variants: 38:1 'set your house in order' — proverbial-deathbed-counsel; 38:5 'fifteen years' added to Hezekiah's life; 38:8 SUNDIAL-OF-AHAZ shadow-back-ten-degrees miracle; 38:9–20 Hezekiah's-poetic-psalm (LXX-distinctive — only-here, not-in-2-Kings).
preamble.structural_notes: MT Isaiah 38 = LXX Isaiah 38. 22 verses. // 2 Kings 20:1–11.

variant_notes: 'In those days Hezekiah became sick and was at the point of death. And Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz came to him, and said to him: Thus says the LORD: Set your house in order, for you shall die, you shall not recover' tracks MT. SET-YOUR-HOUSE-IN-ORDER deathbed-counsel.
'Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD' tracks MT. TURNED-HIS-FACE-TO-WALL — private-grief-and-prayer posture.
'And said: Please, O LORD, remember how I have walked before you in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in your sight. And Hezekiah wept bitterly' tracks MT.
'Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah' tracks MT.

'Go and say to Hezekiah: Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your life' tracks MT. FIFTEEN-YEARS extension. Prayer-changes-divine-decree (within-divine-foreordained-mystery).
'I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and will defend this city' tracks MT.
'This shall be the sign to you from the LORD, that the LORD will do this thing that he has promised' tracks MT.

'Behold, I will make the shadow cast by the declining sun on the dial of Ahaz turn back ten steps. So the sun turned back on the dial the ten steps by which it had declined' tracks MT. SUNDIAL-OF-AHAZ shadow-reversal. The-most-physically-extraordinary miracle in-Isaiah. Joshua's-sun-standing-still (Josh 10:13) parallels.

'A writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, after he had been sick and had recovered from his sickness' tracks MT. HEZEKIAH'S PSALM begins (vv. 9–20). Unique-to-Isaiah, absent-from-2-Kings parallel-account.
'I said: In the middle of my days I must depart; I am consigned to the gates of Sheol for the rest of my years' tracks MT. GATES-OF-SHEOL — Matt 16:18's 'gates of hell' parallel.

'I said: I shall not see the LORD, the LORD in the land of the living; I shall look on man no more among the inhabitants of the world' tracks MT. LAND-OF-THE-LIVING (eretz chayyim) — Pss 27:13, 116:9 parallels.

'My dwelling is plucked up and removed from me like a shepherd's tent; like a weaver I have rolled up my life; he cuts me off from the loom; from day to night you bring me to an end' tracks MT. WEAVER-IMAGERY for-life. // Job 7:6's 'days swifter than weaver's shuttle.'
'I calmed myself until morning; like a lion he breaks all my bones; from day to night you bring me to an end' tracks MT.

'Like a swallow or a crane I chirp; I moan like a dove. My eyes are weary with looking upward. O Lord, I am oppressed; be my pledge of safety!' tracks MT. BE-MY-PLEDGE — surety-cry. Hebrews 7:22 ('Jesus has become the GUARANTOR of a better covenant') Christologically-extends.
'What shall I say? For he has spoken to me, and he himself has done it. I walk slowly all my years because of the bitterness of my soul' tracks MT.
'O Lord, by these things men live, and in all these is the life of my spirit. Oh restore me to health and make me live!' tracks MT.

'Behold, it was for my welfare that I had great bitterness; but in love you have delivered my life from the pit of destruction, for you have cast all my sins behind your back' tracks MT. CAST-SINS-BEHIND-YOUR-BACK. Forgiveness-imagery. Micah 7:19 ('cast all our sins into the depths of the sea') parallel.

'For Sheol does not thank you; death does not praise you; those who go down to the pit do not hope for your faithfulness' tracks MT. PRE-RESURRECTION SHEOL theology. // Pss 6:5, 30:9, 88:10–12. The book-of-Isaiah elsewhere transcends-this in-26:19.
'The living, the living, he thanks you, as I do this day; the father makes known to the children your faithfulness' tracks MT. LIVING-LIVING DOUBLED. Inter-generational-faithfulness.
'The LORD will save me, and we will play my music on stringed instruments all the days of our lives, at the house of the LORD' tracks MT.
'Now Isaiah had said: Let them take a cake of figs and apply it to the boil, that he may recover' tracks MT. FIG-CAKE remedy — Isaiah-as-physician.
'Hezekiah also had said: What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of the LORD?' tracks MT.
